"I'm timing contractions using BabyCentre's My Pregnancy & Baby Today app. Here's what's happening!"

"

Timing your contractions

A contraction is the tightening of your uterine muscles. Women experience contractions in all kinds of ways, ranging from cramping, tightening, burning, backache and more.

When you’re in active labour, your contractions will get progressively longer, more powerful and closer together.

Our contraction timer will help you keep track of what you’re experiencing. When a contraction begins, press “Start contraction” and when it ends, press “Stop contraction.” We’ll record the information for you and calculate the average length and time between your contractions.

You should phone your midwife once you think you’re in active labour, but don’t be embarrassed to call if you’re unsure. Your midwife will want to know how close together your contractions are and how long they last.

If your waters break during the early part of labour or if you experience any bleeding, contact your doctor or midwife right away.

If this isn’t your first baby or if you feel your labour is progressing very quickly, you might need to contact your midwife sooner."

"When your baby is most active, press “start timer” and then the “kick” button every time you feel your baby kick, turn, or move. The tool tracks how long it takes to record 10 movements and saves each session so you can compare.
Try to track your baby’s movements at the same time each day.

It’s important to remember that there’s no set number of movements you should feel each day; every baby is different. The important thing is to get to know your baby's usual movements from day to day. If you haven’t felt your little one move by 24 weeks, inform your midwife. Also, if you notice a change or reduction in your baby’s movements, speak to your midwife."
